subject: Hosted inference advisory: prefetch fanout congestion in us-east
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@lumosai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference advisory: prefetch fanout congestion in us-east

Hi Jane / LumosAI team,

We detected an increase in queued work and higher p95 response times for a subset of hosted inference requests serving the us-east region between ~08:42–09:10 PDT this morning. Root cause appears to be an unexpected fanout from our prefetch/cold-start logic that amplified KV-cache invalidations across a small number of placement groups, which in turn caused transient blocking on the request dispatch path.

What you may have observed:
- Short-lived p95 latency increases (observed peak ~2.4s) for ~3% of requests routed to your account’s model route.
- A small number of streaming responses experienced delayed first tokens.
- No evidence of model quality regressions or incorrect outputs.

What we did:
- Immediately activated a conservative fallback policy to route affected traffic to a compatible model variant that does not use aggressive prefetch. That preserved correctness while reducing tail latency.
- Increased autoscaler buffer for the affected placement groups and applied a temporary throttling cap on prefetch concurrency.
- Opened an internal bridge and traced a timeline; early indicators point at a concurrency regression introduced in yesterday’s runtime change to prefetch prioritization.

Next steps for Redwood:
- We’re preparing a concise incident timeline and a postmortem draft (will share by EOD PT).
- We will propose remediation (rollback of the prioritization change + improved prefetch caps) and a follow-up plan to prevent recurrence.

Immediate ask for LumosAI:
- If you continue to see elevated latencies, reply with recent request IDs (x-request-id header) or representative traces and we’ll prioritize them.

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll follow up shortly with the incident timeline and the link to the status page update.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:45:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference advisory: prefetch fanout congestion in us-east

Hi Jane — thanks for the questions. Short answers up front:
- Estimated affected volume: ~2.8% of routed requests for LumosAI during the window (we observed ~18k requests total for your account in the window; ~500–600 showed elevated tail latency).
- Errors: We saw a small number (~12) of 5xx responses tied to queue timeouts; the vast majority were higher-latency 2xx responses. No data corruption or model-output issues.
- Billing/SLO: The fallback routes to a compatible variant with slightly higher median latency but identical token accounting; we will not change token billing. If you want us to exclude the impacted interval from SLA calculations or discuss a goodwill credit, we can open a formal request.

Technical details / timeline (brief):
- 08:41:53 PT — internal telemetry spike: prefetch queue length increments on placement-group pg-us-east-7.
- 08:42:20 PT — beginning of client-visible latency increase.
- 08:45:10 PT — auto-mitigation: conservative fallback routing and prefetch concurrency cap applied.
- 09:06:00 PT — autoscaler buffer fully provisioned; observed p95 trending back to baseline by 09:10 PT.

We’ve attached a CSV timeline and a draft postmortem to this thread. The engineering lead will propose the rollback window and the safe guardrails (prefetch caps + a canary rollout policy) by EOD.

For transparency we will also publish a concise statuspage incident note: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-05-18-prefetch-fanout

If LumosAI would like a short call to review traces and credits, Sean and I can schedule one today.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: incident summary and next steps (prefetch fanout)

Hi Jane / team — following up with the final customer-facing summary and the remediation plan. Thank you again for the quick signals and the request IDs you provided.

Summary:
- Root cause: a regression in the prefetch prioritization logic that allowed concurrent prefetch jobs to fan out across placement groups in us-east and briefly overwhelm dispatch queues.
- Customer impact: ~2.8% of routed requests saw elevated p95 latency between 08:42–09:10 PT on 2027-05-18. ~12 requests returned 5xx due to queue timeouts; no data loss or incorrect outputs.

Remediation (already in progress):
- Immediate mitigation: conservative fallback routing + prefetch concurrency cap (applied 08:45 PT).
- Short-term: rollback of the prefetch prioritization change and a targeted canary to validate behavior before re-release.
- Long-term: introduce per-account prefetch caps, enhanced prefetch queue metrics, and an automated guardrail to prevent cross-placement fanout.

Customer offer:
- We will exclude the impacted interval from SLA calculations on request — or if you prefer, we can apply a one-time goodwill credit. Please indicate which you prefer and the billing contact to coordinate with.

Materials:
- Incident timeline (CSV) and a draft postmortem are attached. Final postmortem will be published to the status page and your account folder after internal review: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-05-18-prefetch-fanout

Would you like us to set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through traces and the proposed rollback schedule? If so, suggest a time and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this with high priority and will share the final postmortem within 48 hours.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
